end.summary:
Explored “unity in diversity” and “many in the one.”
Used harvest festivals, including Pongal, Bihu, Makar Sankranti and Lohri, to identify shared ideas and different foods and customs.
Practised examples of diversity in language, food, dress, festivals and music.
Riya explained that different people can live together, share and learn while celebrating in different ways.
Teach-back was not passed; music examples and the final festival comparison needed further support.
end.parentNote: Riya practised finding a common idea among different festivals, foods, languages, clothing and musical instruments. They used the shared harvest-season idea and examples such as til-gud and rewri, and explained that people can celebrate together in different ways. They initially mixed up whether festivals have the same meaning or the same customs; this was clarified later when they noted that the seasonal idea can be common while rituals and foods differ. At home, ask Riya to make a four-column list—language, food, dress and festival—with two different examples and one shared idea for each.
